newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil opposition makes progress toward CVRD probe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil opposition makes progress toward CVRD probe.

text.p: Left-wing opponents of the privatization of Brazilian mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) said they had made progress in mustering support for an inquiry into the $5.0 billion sell-off.

Workers Party deputy Joao Fassarella said about 180 members of the Chamber of Deputies had signed a petition calling for a Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry (CPI) into the upcoming CVRD sale, more than the 171 signatures needed in the lower house.
But the opposition parties also require support from one-third of Brazil's Senate before the CPI probe can be set up.
Senator Junia Marise of the Democratic Workers Party, in charge of gathering the signatures in the upper house, was not available for comment.
Fassarella said he did not know how many senators had signed up, but expected the upper house to prove less enthusiastic on a CPI than the Chamber of Deputies.
"The government is going to use all its strength to make sure the inquiry doesn't take place," Fassarella said.

The backers of a probe need support in the Senate as well. A joint Chamber-Senate inquiry is sought for scheduling reasons. A bicameral investigation could probably be carried out ahead of the CVRD sale late next month, while the lower house has too many other investigations on its slate to accommodate the CVRD probe ahead of the auction date.
The probe would look into an alleged conflict of interest involving U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch, which acted as consultant to the Brazilian government on the CVRD privatization.

Left-wing members of Congress have alleged Merrill Lynch's ownership of a Johannesburg-based brokerage, which works for South African mining conglomerate and expected CVRD bidder Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, represents a conflict of interest.
Merrill Lynch has denied the allegation.
The privatization of CVRD is due to begin April 29 with the sale of 40-45 percent of the company's voting shares.
